quote:
GTA 6 – 13 Years, Billions of Dollars, and Somehow This Is the Result?

I honestly expected far more from Grand Theft Auto VI. After roughly 13 years of waiting, an enormous development budget, and one of the biggest marketing campaigns in gaming history, this release feels incredibly disappointing. At this point, I have to question what all those years and resources were actually spent on.

One of my biggest issues is the game's seemingly insensitive treatment of Islam. Describing a strip club as the “Mekka of rich people” is an incredibly questionable choice of wording. Mecca (Makkah) is the holiest city in Islam, and comparing it to a strip club associated with wealth, sexual entertainment, and hedonism is disrespectful to a religion followed by billions of people. Satire is one thing, but there should still be a level of awareness and consideration when referencing religious symbols and sacred places. This just comes across as unnecessary and offensive.

The excessive nudity and sexual content are another major problem. GTA has always been provocative, but there is a difference between mature content that serves a purpose and content that feels excessive simply for the sake of shock value. At times, it feels as though the game relies too heavily on sexualization rather than delivering meaningful substance.

And then we get to the bugs and glitches. After 13 flipping years of development, how is a release with this many technical problems acceptable? This isn't some small indie project developed by a handful of people on a shoestring budget. This is Rockstar Games, backed by an enormous budget and years upon years of development time. Players have every right to expect a polished, stable experience. Spending over a decade developing a game and still having it launch with frustrating bugs, glitches, and technical inconsistencies is genuinely embarrassing.

The budget makes all of this even harder to justify. With hundreds of millions—potentially approaching or exceeding a billion dollars in total development and marketing costs depending on what figures are included—this should have been an exceptionally polished product. Instead, it feels like certain aspects were prioritized over quality control, common sense, and creative restraint.

After 13 years of anticipation, I expected something that would redefine gaming, not something that leaves me disappointed by its writing, excessive sexual content, and technical shortcomings. The amount of hype surrounding this game makes its flaws even more noticeable.

13 years. An absurd budget. Endless hype. And yet, somehow, this is what we got. The name GTA and Rockstar shouldn't be a free pass for criticism. **** takes this long and costs this much to make, it should deliver excellence—not excuses.
